title: Fidelity Staging SDK and Eval Playbook (PRD)
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This PRD defines the Fidelity Staging SDK and associated evaluation playbook: a lightweight developer-facing toolkit and process to enable customers and internal teams to stage, test, and certify fidelity configurations (quantization, caching, batching, model variants) against representative prompt sets before rollout. The goal is to reduce fidelity regressions in production, speed up onboarding to fidelity tiers, and provide repeatable telemetry-driven pass/fail gates for rollouts.

Goals:
- Provide a cross-platform SDK (Python + Node) for running staged inference locally or against a dedicated staging endpoint with configurable fidelity profiles.
- Ship a standard eval harness that runs customer or internal prompt sets, captures quality regressions (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-similarity where applicable), and correlates with cost/latency telemetry.
- Define a playbook with concrete gating criteria (metrics, thresholds, sample sizes) for canary and staged rollouts.
- Integrate telemetry hooks and export formats compatible with Console and Optimize for downstream dashboards and alerts.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not replace full model training or large-scale offline evaluation labs.
- It does not directly implement automatic rollback; the playbook produces signals for deployment tooling to act on.

Target users and personas:
- Developer/ML engineer onboarding to Dedicated or Private deployments who need to validate fidelity settings before production.
- Solutions and SE teams running proofs-of-concept for customers.
- Internal SRE and QA teams validating release variants for safety and regressions.

High-level product features:
1) Fidelity Staging SDK (Python, Node)
   - API: client.fidelity.stage(profile_id, prompt_set_id, options) -> run_id
   - Profiles: declarative fidelity profiles (YAML/JSON) describing model variant, quantization level, batch policy, kv-cache policy, and fallback order.
   - Local simulator mode: run a small in-memory runtime that mimics batching/caching behavior for low-cost validation.
   - Remote staging mode: run tests against a customer-dedicated staging endpoint (hosted or private).
   - Export: standardized result bundle (.tar.gz) containing outputs, token-level timings, and telemetry manifest.

2) Eval Harness and Metrics
   - Pluggable metric plugins: text-match (exact, token-level), ROUGE, BLEU, embedding-sim (cosine, dot), rank correlation for reranking tasks, and custom JS/Python validator hooks.
   - Quality drift detection: baseline vs candidate comparison, bootstrap confidence intervals, and a summary regression score.
   - Cost/latency correlation: per-sample token count, per-token latency distribution, batching efficiency, and per-request fallback events.

3) Playbook: Staging -> Canary -> Production
   - Stage: run full prompt-set eval (recommended N >= 500 for transactional apps, N >= 2k for large conversational datasets) in staging with fidelity profile A and baseline profile B; generate result bundle and telemetry.
   - Gate: automated pass/fail rules (see gating matrix below).
   - Canary: if Stage passes, schedule canary with 5–10% traffic for 24–72 hours with focused telemetry hooks.
   - Promote or rollback: manual review + automated alerts triggered by exceedance of fail-thresholds.

Gating matrix (summary table):
| Dimension | Metric | Baseline | Acceptable delta | Action if exceeded | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Quality (text) | Median ROUGE-L | baseline_value | -2.0 points | Fail stage | For summarization workloads |
| Quality (semantic) | Embedding cosine (mean) | baseline_value | -0.02 | Fail stage | Use domain-specific embedding model |
| Latency | p95 per-token latency | baseline_value | +30% | Canary only | We permit short p95 increases if cost improves |
| Cost | Cost per 1k tokens | baseline_value | -10% (improvement) or +15% (degradation) | Flag for review | Business decision for acceptance |
| Fallbacks | Fallback count per 1k requests | 0 | > 5 | Fail stage | Fallbacks indicate compatibility issues |

Implementation milestones (high-level timeline):
1. 2026-10-15: Tech spike & API contract (Python + Node prototypes)
2. 2026-11-12: Eval harness v1 with ROUGE/embedding plugins and local simulator
3. 2026-11-30: Integration with staging endpoints + export bundle spec
4. 2026-12-15: Playbook draft and gating automation scripts (CI)
5. 2026-12-22: Internal launch for SE and SRE trial (this PRD target)
6. 2027-01-20: Public docs + sample prompt-sets and developer quickstart

Rollout and launch plan:
- Phase 0 (Internal trial): limited to two SE teams and internal SRE; collect feedback over 2 weeks. Owner: Solutions Eng (SE).
- Phase 1 (Early customers): onboard 3 pilot customers (one AI-native startup, one mid-market SaaS, one enterprise with Private deployment) for staged use within their sandbox; duration 4 weeks. Owner: Customer Success + SE.
- Phase 2 (General availability): SDK published, Console flows to upload result bundles and gating status visible in per-route dashboards. Owner: Product + DevEx.

SLOs and thresholds for the staging service (staging endpoints and SDK telemetry ingestion):
- SDK CLI: <5s cold start for Python package operations (install + first-run) on standard dev workstation.
- Telemetry ingestion: 99.9% of events processed within 30s of completion for staging runs under 10k samples.
- Eval harness run success rate: 99% on supported prompt-set formats (JSONL, CSV).

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Product: overall PRD owner, success metrics, go-to-market materials. (Owner: Maya Chen)
- Eng (Runtime): implement staging endpoint compatibility and fallback telemetry hooks. (Lead: Arjun Patel)
- Eng (DevEx): SDKs and examples (Python, Node). (Lead: Priya Kapoor)
- Customer Success/SE: pilot coordination and prompt-set guidance.
- SRE: telemetry pipeline and ingestion SLOs.

APIs and manifest examples (sketch):
- fidelity_profile.yaml (example):
  name: "compact-quant-8"
  model_variant: "redwood-compact-v1"
  quantization: q8
  batching: {max_batch_tokens: 4096, prefer_latency: true}
  kv_cache: {enabled: true, ttl_seconds: 3600}
  fallback_order: ["redwood-compact-v1", "redwood-compact-v1-lr" ]

- Sample CLI flows:
  $ rwd-fidelity stage --profile fidelity_profile.yaml --prompt-set prompts/customer-sentiment.jsonl --mode remote --output bundle.tar.gz
  $ rwd-fidelity analyze --bundle bundle.tar.gz --metrics embedding_cosine,rouge_l --out report.html

Telemetry events (minimum fields):
- fidelity.run.start {run_id, profile_id, prompt_set_id, timestamp, run_mode} 
- fidelity.sample.result {run_id, sample_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, fallback_taken, model_variant, output_hash} 
- fidelity.run.summary {run_id, metrics:{...}, cost_estimate_usd, exported_bundle_url} 

QA and acceptance criteria:
- SDK unit/integration tests covering profile parsing, local simulator behavior, and result bundle creation.
- Eval harness reproducibility: repeated runs on same seed produce deterministic metric buckets within noise thresholds.
- Telemetry manifests accepted by Console ingestion (schema validation).
- Pilot customers can run a full stage -> canary cycle within 48h and produce a pass/fail report.

Security and compliance:
- Sensitive prompt text must be redacted in exported bundles unless customer explicitly enables retention (opt-in).
- Bundles stored in staging S3 must honor tenant encryption keys (KMS integration).
- Access controls: stage runs in Private deployments respect VPC and KMS boundaries.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: False positives on quality regressions due to brittle metrics.
  Mitigation: support multiple metric plugins and require consensus across at least two metrics for a hard fail.
- Risk: Large prompt sets exceed telemetry ingestion capacity.
  Mitigation: sampling guidance, backpressure on SDK, and batch-upload retry semantics.

Open questions for review:
1. What should be the minimum recommended prompt-set size by workload type? (proposal: 500 transactional, 2k conversational, 10k retrieval-heavy)
2. Is an automated rollback desirable at first launch or deferred to a later stage?
3. Storage TTL for exported bundles by default (proposal: 30 days for staging, configurable per-customer).

Appendix: Example report summary (text):
- Run 2026-11-18-1234 (profile: compact-quant-8)
  - samples: 2,000
  - mean embedding cosine vs baseline: 0.944 (delta -0.014) -> flag (soft)
  - median ROUGE-L: 43.2 (delta -0.6) -> pass
  - p95 latency per-token: +12% -> pass
  - cost per 1k tokens: -18% -> positive
  - fallback events: 0 -> pass
  - recommendation: proceed to 7% canary with additional human review on embedding drift
